transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been struggling a lot with following through on instructions and actually finishing my tasks at work and home. I'll start chores or projects but almost never seem to complete them, and I keep forgetting my basic daily responsibilities. It's just getting really hard to manage everything.
Do you also often feel very restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or act impulsively before thinking?

Yes, absolutely. I'm constantly fidgeting, tapping my hands or feet, and squirming around in my chair. I also really struggle to stay seated during meetings or dinners and find myself getting up and leaving my seat quite often.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation), Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)], but the new history clearly adds prominent hyperactive/restless symptoms (constant fidgeting, inability to stay seated, getting up often), so Predominantly Inattentive Presentation is less likely and Combined Presentation is the best fit.

inference_history.note: Previously there were no candidates provided, and based on this initial report the main concern is chronic inattention with difficulty following through, completing tasks, and forgetting responsibilities. This most strongly suggests ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation. Combined presentation remains possible because we do not yet have enough information to rule in or out hyperactive/impulsive symptoms.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports clear inattentive symptoms (difficulty following through, incomplete tasks, forgetfulness, poor management of responsibilities) along with hyperactive symptoms (constant fidgeting, squirming, difficulty staying seated, frequent leaving seat).
